lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Special Places: Mosques and More
lesson.summary: Visit the mosque and learn how it is a place of prayer and community, then see other places of worship.
learning_objectives: Name parts and uses of a mosque
Show respect for other places of worship

standards.text: Recognise some religious and non-religious places of worship; understand what happens there; show respect for others' beliefs

success_criteria: I can name parts of a mosque
I can say why Friday is special
I can show respect in any place of worship
lesson.real_life: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore and the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, a local mosque in the UK, mosque open days, and shared community events.

warm_up.prompt: What do we say to thank someone?
We should be kind to people of all faiths.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: why are places of worship special?
blocks.say: Today we learn about special places where people pray. We start with the mosque.

blocks.alt: A large red sandstone mosque with white marble domes and four tall minarets around a wide courtyard
blocks.caption: The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, with its domes and minarets.
blocks.credit: Photo by Jamshaid Mughal on Unsplash
blocks.say: This is the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore. It has red walls, domes and tall minarets.

blocks.markdown: **Salah** is the Muslim prayer. A mosque is a place of **worship**.
blocks.say: A mosque is a place where Muslims pray together. We call the prayer salah.

blocks.markdown: The **mihrab** shows the direction to pray.
blocks.say: Inside is a big prayer hall. A small curved space, the mihrab, shows the way to Makkah.

scenes.caption: Prayer hall.
scenes.say: The prayer hall is a big, quiet room with soft carpet.

scenes.caption: Mihrab.
scenes.say: The mihrab is a curved space in the wall. It shows the way to Makkah.

scenes.caption: Minaret.
scenes.say: The minaret is a tall tower. The call to prayer is called from there.

question.explanation: The mihrab shows the direction of prayer.

blocks.alt: Close-up of a woven rug with a red, blue and cream floral pattern
blocks.caption: A woven rug with a beautiful pattern. Many mosques have soft patterned carpets.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ashkan Forouzani on Unsplash
blocks.say: Before salah, Muslims make wudu. They wash hands, face and feet with clean water.

blocks.markdown: **Wudu** is the washing done before prayer.
blocks.say: We take off our shoes before we step on the carpet. This keeps the floor clean.

scenes.caption: Wudu.
scenes.say: First, we make wudu with clean water.

scenes.caption: Shoes off.
scenes.say: Next, we leave our shoes at the door.

scenes.caption: Rows.
scenes.say: Then, we stand together in rows to pray.

question.prompt: We take our shoes off before we walk on the mosque carpet.
question.explanation: Shoes come off at the mosque door.

blocks.title: Omar's Friday and the open day
blocks.transcript: It is Friday. Omar goes to Jummah with Abbu. First they make wudu with clean water. They take off their shoes at the door. Inside, the mihrab shows the way to Makkah. After prayer, neighbours greet each other. On Saturday, Omar visits a church open day. He walks quietly, listens and asks polite questions. Every place of worship deserves respect.
blocks.caption: Omar goes with Abbu to Jummah prayer and then meets a friend at a local church open day.

points: A mosque is a place of worship
The mihrab shows the way to Makkah
We make wudu and take off our shoes
blocks.say: Let us remember. A mosque is a place of prayer. We wash and take off shoes before we pray.

blocks.say: Friday is a special day. Muslims gather at the mosque for Jummah prayer.

scenes.caption: The call.
scenes.say: At noon on Friday, the call to prayer is made. People gather.

scenes.caption: The talk.
scenes.say: The imam gives a short talk. Then everyone prays together.

scenes.caption: Greetings.
scenes.say: After prayer, people greet each other and share kind words.

question.hint: It is called the day of gathering.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Who comes to the mosque?

blocks.markdown: A mosque brings a community together.
blocks.say: A mosque is also a community place. Families, friends and neighbours come.

scenes.caption: Learning.
scenes.say: Families come to pray and to learn the Quran.

scenes.caption: Volunteers.
scenes.say: Neighbours meet. Volunteers help to keep the mosque clean.

scenes.caption: Some cannot.
scenes.say: Some people cannot go every Friday. They may be ill or travelling.

blocks.say: When we visit a mosque, we show respect. Good manners help everyone.

scenes.caption: Quiet.
scenes.say: Take off your shoes. Walk quietly.

scenes.caption: Dress.
scenes.say: Dress modestly. Cover arms and legs, and cover hair if you wish.

scenes.caption: Listen.
scenes.say: Do not run. Do not shout. Listen to the guide.

question.prompt: Which is good manners in a mosque?
question.explanation: We walk quietly in a mosque.
